title: Consequences Analysis of Liquid Hydrogen Storage Tank Leakage at Urban Hydrogen Refueling Stations: A Case Study
content: Hydrogen energy is considered a crucial clean energy carrier for replacing fossil fuels. Liquid hydrogen (LH2), noted for its economic advantages and high purity, is central to the development of future hydrogen refueling stations (HRSs). However, leakage poses significant fire and explosion risks, which challenge its safe use. In this study, a numerical model of LH2 leakage at an HRS in Chongqing was established using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) software. It examines the diffusion law of a flammable gas cloud (FGC) under the synergistic effect of leakage direction, rate, and wind speed of a LH2 storage tank in a HRS. The phase transition of LH2 presents dual risks of combustion and frostbite owing to the spatial overlap of low-temperature areas and FGCs. The findings reveal that the equivalent stoichiometric gas cloud volume reaches 685 m3 in cases of crosswind leakage, with the superimposed effect of LH2 transport vehicle reflected waves resulting in a peak explosion overpressure of 0.61 bar, posing a significant risk of fatalities. These research outcomes offer crucial theoretical underpinning for enhancing equipment layout optimizations and safety protection strategies at HRSs.
